title: Split Array into Fibonacci Sequence
notes:
## Intuition

Once the first two numbers are chosen, the whole rest of the split is forced: each next piece must spell exactly the sum of the previous two. So the only real choices are where each piece ends, and most choices die quickly. Backtracking tries piece lengths from left to right and abandons a branch as soon as a piece breaks a rule. A brute force that tries every pair of first two pieces and then follows the forced chain gives the same answers.

## Approach

1. Keep the pieces chosen so far in `sequence` and call `backtrack(0)`.
2. In `backtrack(start)`, reaching the end of `num` is a success only if `sequence` has at least 3 numbers.
3. Grow a candidate `value` one digit at a time with `end`. Stop when the piece would have a leading zero, exceed `LIMIT`, or already exceed the sum of the last two numbers (adding digits only makes it larger).
4. Accept `value` when fewer than two numbers are chosen or it equals that sum: push it, recurse on `end + 1`, and pop it if the recursion fails.
5. Return `sequence` on success, otherwise an empty list.

## Example 1, step by step

For `num = "1101111"`: the first piece `1` and second piece `1` need a third piece `2`, but the next digit is `0`, so that fails. Second piece `10` gives `11` next, then needs `21` but sees `11`. Longer second pieces overshoot. Back at the start, the first piece `11` with second piece `0` needs `11` (found) and then `11` (found), which uses every digit: the answer is `[11, 0, 11, 11]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n), where n = `num.length`, with a sizeable constant: only about 10 lengths fit under `LIMIT` for each of the first two pieces, and after them every piece is forced, so each of those ~100 starts scans the rest of the string once.
- Space: O(n) for `sequence` and the recursion depth.

## Pitfalls

- Values must stay below 2^31: check `value > LIMIT` before comparing, or a long piece can look like a valid sum.
- `"0"` is a legal piece, but `"01"` is not; break as soon as a longer piece starts with `0`.
- Reaching the end of the string with only two numbers is not a success.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `LIMIT` | largest allowed value, 2^31 - 1 |
| `sequence` | the pieces chosen so far, as numbers |
| `start` | index where the next piece begins |
| `end` | index of the last digit of the current candidate piece |
| `value` | the candidate piece `num[start..end]` as a number |
| `size` | how many numbers `sequence` holds |

narration.2: The largest value a piece may have: 2^31 - 1.
narration.3: The pieces chosen so far; it doubles as the answer on success.
narration.7: ...which is a success only with at least three numbers.
narration.10: Try each possible end of the next piece, one digit longer each time.
narration.11: A piece longer than one digit may not start with 0.
narration.14: Append the digit at end to the candidate value.
narration.15: Past the 32-bit limit, and longer pieces only grow, so stop.
narration.19: With two numbers chosen, a value above their sum can only get bigger: stop.
narration.22: The first two pieces are free; later ones must equal the sum exactly.
narration.24: Try to split the rest of the string after it.
narration.25: The rest worked, so report success up the chain.
narration.27: The rest failed: undo the choice and try a longer piece.
narration.30: No length worked from this start.
narration.33: Return the pieces if the whole string split, otherwise an empty list.
